title: Prabhas' Period War Drama Fauzi Locks December 3 Release, Sets Up Year-End Box Office Showdown
excerpt: The Hanu Raghavapudi directorial, mounted on a reported ₹400 crore budget, features Mithun Chakraborty, Anupam Kher, and debutante Imanvi alongside the pan-India superstar.
body:
• Fauzi will release worldwide on December 3, 2026, in Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, and Bengali
  • The film is set in pre-Independence India and follows a British Indian soldier, directed by Sita Ramam filmmaker Hanu Raghavapudi
  • The cast includes Mithun Chakraborty, Anupam Kher, and Jaya Prada alongside newcomer Imanvi as the female lead
  • The December release puts Fauzi in a potential clash with films from Akshay Kumar and Ajay Devgn during the lucrative Christmas window

Release Date Confirmed After Months of Speculation

https://youtube.com/watch?v=djKFgKq9WVc

Pan-India superstar Prabhas's highly anticipated period war drama Fauzi has locked its theatrical release for December 3, 2026. Production house Mythri Movie Makers announced the date alongside a striking new poster that shows Prabhas in a battle-worn avatar — bloodied and seated among fallen soldiers on a war-ravaged battlefield, rifle in hand, with the tagline "A Battalion Who Fights Alone."

"Prabhas plays a soldier in the British Indian Army whose journey intertwines with the freedom struggle."

"Prabhas plays a soldier in the British Indian Army whose journey intertwines with the freedom struggle."

The announcement ends months of speculation about the film's release window. Fauzi had initially been targeting an Independence Day 2026 release before shifting to a Dussehra/November window. The December 3 date positions the film strategically ahead of the Christmas-New Year corridor, historically one of Indian cinema's most lucrative theatrical windows.

Hanu Raghavapudi's Ambitious Vision

Directed by Hanu Raghavapudi, whose 2022 romantic drama Sita Ramam earned widespread critical acclaim, Fauzi is set against the backdrop of pre-Independence India. Prabhas plays a soldier in the British Indian Army whose journey intertwines with the freedom struggle. The film blends large-scale action sequences with an emotionally driven narrative — a signature of Raghavapudi's storytelling approach that pairs sweeping visuals with intimate character moments.

The film marks the acting debut of internet personality Imanvi as the female lead, while veterans Mithun Chakraborty, Anupam Kher, and Jaya Prada take key supporting roles. Music is composed by Vishal Chandrasekhar, who scored Sita Ramam to wide acclaim, with Sudeep Chatterjee handling cinematography.

A ₹400 Crore Gamble

Produced by Mythri Movie Makers in association with T-Series, Fauzi is reportedly mounted on a budget of approximately ₹400 crore, making it one of the most expensive Telugu productions currently in progress. The massive investment reflects both the scale of the period setting and Prabhas's status as one of Indian cinema's biggest commercial draws following the Baahubali franchise and Kalki 2898 AD.

The stakes are high. Prabhas's last release, The Raja Saab, received mixed reviews from critics and audiences. A strong performance from Fauzi is essential to maintaining his box office momentum and the financial viability of mega-budget Indian productions.

December Clash Looms

The December 3 release puts Fauzi in a potential collision with major Hindi films from Akshay Kumar and Ajay Devgn also eyeing the year-end window. Whether all three films hold their dates remains to be seen, but the showdown would test audience appetite for multiple big-ticket releases in a single corridor.

For the global Indian diaspora, Fauzi's multi-language release across six Indian languages ensures wide theatrical availability in international markets. The pan-India release strategy — now standard for Telugu superstar vehicles — reflects the continuing expansion of South Indian cinema's global footprint and the overseas audience's growing appetite for period epics that blend spectacle with Indian historical narratives.
